display.purpose: The owner's name and the five layer names. Uppercase, font-stretch 62%.

headline.purpose: Layer names in the hero bars, the contact question, headings under the stack, the rail monogram. Uppercase, font-stretch 62%.

title.purpose: Entry titles and the button label. font-stretch 87%.

body.purpose: Reading text at normal width, capped at 62ch.

label.purpose: Codes, dates, status flags, rail names, key and footer. Uppercase, font-stretch 75%; never monospace.

shadows.name: target-spread
shadows.purpose: Not elevation: an unblurred spread that widens the tint behind a targeted entry.

shadows.name: bar-current
shadows.purpose: Not elevation: the current-segment marker on the narrow top bar (ink on the contact segment).

motion.name: ease-settle
motion.purpose: The one easing curve: bar entrance, rail segment growth, bar hover slide, link arrow nudge. A repeated literal in the build, not a custom property.

motion.name: settle
motion.value: 0.8s, from opacity 0 and translateY(-34px), delay calc(var(--i) * 80ms + 120ms)
motion.purpose: Hero stack bars settle once on load, bottom bar first. The only entrance animation.

motion.name: duration-state
motion.purpose: Rail segment growth and layer-bar hover slide.

motion.name: duration-quick
motion.purpose: Button fill and link underline colour.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: animation: none; transition: none; scroll-behavior: auto
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion the entrance and every transition are removed.

narrative.overview:
The page is drawn as an engineering stack diagram that happens to be a portfolio. Five full-bleed colour fields run from Autonomy at the top to RF at the bottom, each one a step darker than the one above it, and the work sits inside the layer it was done at. The same five bands appear three times at three scales: as the hero diagram, as the fixed rail that navigates the page, and as the sections themselves. Nothing else on the page competes with that one picture.

The surface is flat, square and dense with fact. Structure comes from colour fields and 1.5px rules, never from boxes; hierarchy comes from one typeface changing width, never from a second family. One vermilion signal marks what a visitor can act on or should notice, and it is the only colour outside the blue-green ramp.
keyCharacteristics: Five tonal fields in one hue family, ordered light to dark, each tied to one layer of the stack
A single typeface (Archivo) worked along its width axis: 62%, 75%, 87%, 100%
Square corners, 1.5px rules, full-bleed bands; no cards, no elevation
One signal colour, used for action, thread, status and position
Still by default: one entrance animation, then state changes only

rules.name: The Depth Is Meaning Rule
rules.body: A ramp step is a layer of the stack. `f5` to `f1` appear only in stack order and only to mean their layer; they are never picked for decoration, contrast or variety.

rules.name: The Field Sets The Ink Rule
rules.body: A component never names its own colours. It reads four local values from the field it sits on (field, text, secondary text, rule), so the same entry markup is correct on paper and on all five layers.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Vermilion means "act here", "this continues elsewhere", "status" or "you are here". If a use fits none of those, it does not get the signal.

rules.name: The Width Not Family Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is made by moving along Archivo's width axis and weight, not by adding a typeface. The label voice is condensed caps; it is never monospace.

rules.name: The Caps Are Names Rule
rules.body: Uppercase is for names and labels only: the owner, a layer, a code, a date. Anything a visitor reads as a sentence is sentence case at normal width.

rules.name: The Flat Stack Rule
rules.body: A surface is distinguished from its neighbour by its field colour or by a rule. Blur, offset shadows and translucent overlays are not part of this system.

dos: Do place new work inside the layer it belongs to and let that layer's field colour it; split work that spans layers and join the parts with thread links.
Do build components from the four local field values so they hold on paper and all five layers without overrides.
Do separate items with a 1.5px rule in the field's rule colour and full-bleed bands.
Do set names in 62% width, weight 800 caps, entry titles in 87% width, labels in 75% width semibold caps, and reading text at normal width.
Do switch markers to Signal Light on `f2` and `f1`, and the focus ring to white on dark and signal fields.
Do keep every interactive target at 44px or taller where it is a primary action, and honour `prefers-reduced-motion` by removing the entrance and all transitions.
donts: Don't use a ramp colour out of stack order or for anything other than its layer.
Don't add a second accent, or use the signal as body text or as decoration.
Don't add a second typeface, including a monospace for codes and tool lists.
Don't round corners, box content into cards, or use blurred or offset shadows.
Don't add scroll-triggered or looping motion; the bars settling once on load is the only entrance.
Don't wrap bands in a max-width container; constrain text by measure instead.
